method: wall-clock of `yavo build` per benchmark source, 7 samples, median; warm = unchanged source after one build; edit = a new comment line inserted at line 1 before each build (shifts lines, so generated C changes: cache miss); no_cache = YAVO_NO_CACHE=1
conclusion: The cache removes the back end for unchanged code (warm builds 2-10 ms). It does not help the edit-compile loop, where the generated C always changes: release 214-247 ms (above the 200 ms target), debug 159 ms. About 50-60 ms of each miss is recompiling the 1759-line runtime header; a precompiled runtime object per target/mode is the next lever.
